implementation_notes: Go ships the engine in the standard library: parse a template set with template.ParseFiles/ParseGlob (or New(...).Parse(...)), execute it with Execute/ExecuteTemplate into an io.Writer - normally the http.ResponseWriter - and pass a struct as the dot. html/template escapes every value according to its context (HTML text, attribute, JS, CSS, URL), so XSS defence is the default, while text/template is the same mechanism without escaping for non-HTML output. Parse once at startup and execute per request; the classic view/handler roles collapse into preparing the view struct and calling Execute.
pitfalls: Execute fails halfway if a field or template is missing - after headers and part of the page are written - so render into a bytes.Buffer when a clean error response matters.
template.HTML/JS/URL typed values and the safe-attr helpers disable escaping; converting untrusted strings to those types reintroduces XSS.
ParseFiles names templates after their base file name and ParseGlob order is unspecified: build sets with template.New(...).ParseFiles(...) when names can collide.
